Lohmiller-Midway silty loams, undulating (4 to 15 percent slopes) (LV)
This complex comprises undulating soils on shale hills that border river and intermittent stream valleys. Slopes are mainly 4 to 8 percent but range upward to 15 percent. It is composed of low knolls and ridges of Midway silty clay loam surrounded by smoothly sloping patches of Lohmiller silty clay loam. The highest knolls and ridges rise to 15 to 30 feet above the Lohmiller soils. Slopes are 4 to 10 percent on the Lohmiller soil and 10 to 15 percent on the Midway soil. About 75 percent is Lohmiller silty clay loam and about 25 percent is Midway silty clay loam.
The Lohmiller and Midway soils in this complex have profiles similar to those described for their respective series. Included in the mapping are spots where the Lohmiller soil is underlain by shale at depths of 3 to 5 feet.
This complex is suited to range. Irregular shape and small size areas make the Lohmiller soil unsuitable for cropland.
(Capability Unit IVe-3 Dryland; Clayey range site 10-14 inch precipitation zone; Windbreak Suitability Group 2M).
